mainTopic: A debtor who paid back only part of his loan: do we write a new שטר or a שובר (receipt)?
overview: This amud opens with the last lines of an earlier story. A sage explains that he only meant the litigant should try to verify his claims, not that he automatically loses. Then a new משנה begins: a borrower has paid back part of his loan. רבי יהודה says the lender should swap the old שטר for a new one. רבי יוסי says the lender keeps the old שטר and writes the borrower a שובר (receipt). רבי יהודה objects that the borrower would then have to guard his receipt from mice, and רבי יוסי answers that this is better than weakening the lender. In the גמרא, רב הונא quotes רב: the הלכה follows neither. Instead, the בית דין tears up the old שטר and writes a new one dated from the original date. רב נחמן (or רב ירמיה בר אבא) argues that a ברייתא gives this very method as רבי יהודה's view, so רב would have taken back his ruling. רב הונא answers that רב knew the ברייתא and still kept his ruling. The reason is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: The objection: he only meant 'go verify'
steps.stepSummary: The last line of an objection from the earlier story. The source being quoted only told the litigant to verify his claims, nothing more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he say anything except that he must verify!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of an argument that started before this section. The objector (רבי אבא) insists that the earlier ruling only told the litigant to verify his claims. It never said he loses if he can't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fight is about how strong the earlier ruling was. Does 'go verify' mean 'prove it or you lose'? Or does it just mean 'try to prove it if you can'? The objector reads it the weaker way.

keyTerms.meaning: to verify, to clarify or prove a claim

phrases.english: Did he say anything except to verify!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the argument from the previous page between רבי אבא and רבי יצחק נפחא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The demand that the litigant prove his extra claims
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source only says 'to verify.' It never says the litigant loses if he can't verify.

steps.title: The answer: I also only meant 'verify'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא answers that he never meant anything more. He too only meant that the litigant should verify if he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I too am only saying 'verify.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא agrees with the objector. He explains that his own ruling was never harsher than 'go verify if you can.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: There turns out to be no real argument. Both sides agree the litigant is asked to verify his claims. If he can't, he does not have to pay just because of that. This closes the earlier story.
steps.whatToRemember: The earlier story ends in agreement: 'go verify' means 'try to prove it.' It does not mean 'you automatically lose.'

phrases.english: He said to him: I too
am saying only to verify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא נָמֵי לְבָרֵר קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 1 by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The objector thought the ruling required proof or else the litigant loses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling only meant 'verify if you can.'

steps.title: The משנה: partial repayment, exchange or receipt?
steps.stepSummary: A debtor paid back part of his loan. רבי יהודה says the lender swaps the שטר for a new one. רבי יוסי says the lender writes a שובר instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone paid back part of his debt, רבי יהודה says the lender should exchange the document, and רבי יוסי says the lender should write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It presents a disagreement about what paperwork to do when a borrower pays back only part of his loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יהודה's plan, the old שטר is replaced by a new one for the smaller amount still owed. Under רבי יוסי's plan, the lender keeps the old שטר for the full amount, and the borrower gets a שובר proving he already paid some of it.

keyTerms.meaning: he should exchange (the שטר for a new one)
a receipt showing a payment was made

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who repaid part of his debt,
Rabbi Yehuda says: He should exchange it,
phrases.notes: The lender trades in the old document for a new one showing only what is still owed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: He should write a receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The earlier story has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: replace the שטר with a new one. רבי יוסי: keep the old שטר and write a שובר.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's objection: the receipt could get eaten by mice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה attacks the שובר plan. Under it, the borrower has to guard his receipt forever, or he may have to pay the full amount again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Then this borrower will have to guard his receipt from the mice!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה challenges רבי יוסי's opinion by pointing out a practical problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender keeps the old שטר for the full amount, the borrower's only protection is the שובר. If the שובר is lost or destroyed, the borrower could be forced to pay again what he already paid. רבי יהודה thinks it is unfair to put that burden on the borrower.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
It turns out that this one must be
phrases.notes: "This one" is the borrower, who is holding the receipt.

phrases.english: guarding his receipt from the mice!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: נִמְצָא זֶה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹמֵר שׁוֹבָרוֹ מִן הָעַכְבָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי's opinion from step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It puts the risk on the borrower. If the receipt is lost, he may pay twice.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's answer: better that than weakening the lender
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that this is fitting for the borrower. It is better than weakening the lender's legal power.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: That is fine for him, and this way the lender's strength is not weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי defends his opinion. He accepts that the borrower carries a risk, but says it is the right choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי admits the borrower must guard his שובר. But a new שטר would weaken the lender's position. Between the two, he prefers to protect the lender.

keyTerms.meaning: it is fitting / good for him

steps.whatToRemember: The argument in the משנה is about who carries the risk: the borrower (רבי יוסי) or the lender (רבי יהודה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
This is fitting for him,
and the strength of this one should not be weakened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כָּךְ יָפֶה לוֹ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the downside but says it is the better choice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Putting the risk on the borrower is unfair.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is fitting for the borrower to carry the risk, so the lender is not weakened.

steps.title: רב: the הלכה follows neither, so the בית דין writes a new שטר
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב: the הלכה follows neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי. The בית דין tears the old שטר and writes a new one dated from the original date.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא said in the name of רב: The הלכה is like neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי. Rather, the court tears the document and writes him a new document dated from the first date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב gives a practical ruling that takes a third path between the two opinions of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהודה, there is no שובר, so the borrower has nothing to guard. But the new שטר keeps the original date, so the lender does not lose his early claim. That answers רבי יוסי's worry. And the בית דין does the writing.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלכה is not (like this opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: Keeping the original date protects the lender's claim on property the borrower sold after the loan was first made.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Huna says that Rav says:
The halakha is not like Rabbi Yehuda
and not like Rabbi Yosei;
rather, the court tears up the document,
and writes for him another document
from the first date.
phrases.notes: The new document carries the old document's date, so the lender keeps his original timing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: אֵין הֲלָכָה לֹא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלֹא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical הלכה on the dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין tears up the old שטר and writes a new one dated from the original date.

steps.title: If רב had known the ברייתא, he would have taken it back
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן (or רב ירמיה בר אבא) tells רב הונא about a ברייתא. It says the עדים tear the שטר and write a new one from the first date. Had רב known it, he would have retracted his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא (some say it was רב ירמיה בר אבא): If רב had heard the ברייתא that teaches 'the witnesses tear up the document and write him another document dated from the first date,' he would have retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב's ruling is being challenged. A ברייתא describes almost the same procedure, so רב's 'third opinion' may not be new after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא presents tear-and-rewrite-from-the-first-date as the method of רבי יהודה's 'exchange'. If so, רב's ruling is not a third path. It is simply רבי יהודה's opinion, so רב would not have said 'the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.' The one difference is that in the ברייתא the עדים do the rewriting, not the בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's method sounds identical to רב's. That is exactly the challenge: the ברייתא gives this method as רבי יהודה's view, so רב seems to be ruling like רבי יהודה after all. The difference between עדים and בית דין is what רב הונא relies on in his answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to Rav Huna,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Yirmeya bar Abba to Rav Huna:
If Rav had heard
this baraita that is taught:
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets, and some leave it out.

phrases.english: The witnesses tear up the document,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוֹתְבִין לוֹ שְׁטָר אַחֵר מִזְּמַן רִאשׁוֹן –
phrases.english: and write for him another document from the first date –
he would have retracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ לְרַב הָא בָּרַיְיתָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 6 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the הלכה follows neither תנא and that the בית דין does the rewriting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא teaches that the tear-and-rewrite method, dated from the first date, is רבי יהודה's view. So רב's ruling is really like רבי יהודה, and he would have retracted his claim that the הלכה follows neither.

steps.title: רב knew the ברייתא and still kept his ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that רב did know the ברייתא and still did not take back his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: רב heard that ברייתא, and he still did not take back his ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back on the claim that רב would have changed his mind. He says רב already knew the ברייתא and kept his ruling anyway. This prepares the next move, where the גמרא explains why רב did not change his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 7 assumed רב simply did not know the ברייתא. רב הונא denies that assumption: רב knew it and still ruled the way he did. In the ruling, the בית דין writes the new שטר, while in the ברייתא the עדים do. So the question now becomes why רב held to his ruling in spite of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He heard it; he knew this source
He took back his ruling; he changed his mind

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב הונא is saying the ברייתא is wrong. He only says רב was aware of it and still held his ruling. The reason comes next.

phrases.english: He said to him: He heard it,
phrases.notes: רב הונא is the one answering here. 'He heard it' means רב already knew that ברייתא.

phrases.english: and he did not retract.
phrases.notes: So רב kept his ruling even though he knew the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ, וְלָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by denying its claim that רב did not know the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenger's assumption that רב did not know the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב must not have known the ברייתא, which presents this very method as רבי יהודה's view. Had he known it, he would have taken back his claim that the הלכה follows neither.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב knew the ברייתא and deliberately kept his ruling, so there must be a reason. The גמרא explains that reason next.
